# Gandhabbakāya Saṁyutta (SN 31)

**ID:** SN 31
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Gandhabbakāya Saṁyutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0303m.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Gandhabbakāya Saṁyutta* (SN 31), translated as the "Linked Discourses on Centaurs", is the thirty-first division of the *Saṁyuttanikāya* [Bodhi 2003]. It constitutes the third of a group of four contiguous collections focused on the conditions and modes under which beings achieve rebirth among various semi-celestial orders [Rhys Davids 1924]. In Buddhist lore, *gandhabbas* are minor deities—often compared to centaurs or fairies—traditionally associated with music, conception, and aromatic vegetation [Rhys Davids 1924; Bodhi 2003]. Throughout the collection, the Buddha explains to questioning monks the causes leading to rebirth in the company of these *gandhabbakāyikā devā* [Rhys Davids 1924; Hazra 1994]. In particular, these beings are described as inhabiting various fragrant botanical parts, including roots, heartwood, pith, bark, sap, leaves, flowers, and scents [Hazra 1994; Bodhi 2003]. According to the commentary, the name is linked to the stem *gandha* ("scent"), and rebirth into specific sub-classes of these beings corresponds systematically to individual gifts of fragrant materials offered by the practitioner [Bodhi 2003].
